source.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹֽנִי־צֶ֜דֶק מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם כִּֽי־לָכַ֨ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ אֶת־הָעַי֮ וַיַּחֲרִימָהּ֒ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה לִֽירִיחוֹ֙ וּלְמַלְכָּ֔הּ כֵּן־עָשָׂ֥ה לָעַ֖י וּלְמַלְכָּ֑הּ וְכִ֨י הִשְׁלִ֜ימוּ יֹשְׁבֵ֤י גִבְעוֹן֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ בְּקִרְבָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when heard Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem that had captured Joshua the Ai and had devoted it to destruction, as he had done to Jericho and to its king so he had done to the Ai and to its king, and that had made peace [the] inhabitants of Gibeon with Israel and were in their midst,

en.L: And it happened, when Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and had devoted it to destruction, that as he had done to Jericho and to its king, so he had done to Ai and to its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were in their midst,
en.B: News reached Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem that Joshua had taken Ai and devoted it to destruction, treating Ai and its king as he had treated Jericho and its king. He also learned that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were now living among them,
en.R: Adoni-Zedek was the king of Jerusalem. He heard that Joshua had captured Ai and destroyed it completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Joshua had done to Ai and its king what he had done to Jericho and its king. Adoni-Zedek also heard that the people of Gibeon had made a peace treaty with Israel and now lived among the Israelites.

sw.L: Ikawa Adoni-sedeki mfalme wa Yerusalemu aliposikia kwamba Yoshua ameuteka Ai na kuuweka wakfu kwa maangamizi, kwamba kama alivyoufanyia Yeriko na mfalme wake, ndivyo alivyoufanyia Ai na mfalme wake, na kwamba wakazi wa Gibeoni wamefanya amani na Israeli na walikuwa katikati yao,
sw.B: Habari zilimfikia Adoni-sedeki mfalme wa Yerusalemu kwamba Yoshua ameuteka Ai na kuuweka wakfu kwa maangamizi, akiutendea Ai na mfalme wake kama alivyoutendea Yeriko na mfalme wake. Alisikia pia kwamba wakazi wa Gibeoni wamefanya amani na Israeli na sasa wanaishi kati yao,
sw.R: Adoni-sedeki alikuwa mfalme wa Yerusalemu. Alisikia kwamba Yoshua ameuteka Ai na kuuangamiza kabisa, kama watu waliotolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Yoshua alikuwa ameutendea Ai na mfalme wake kama alivyoutendea Yeriko na mfalme wake. Adoni-sedeki alisikia pia kwamba watu wa Gibeoni wamefanya mkataba wa amani na Israeli, na sasa wanaishi kati ya Waisraeli.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando Adonisedec, rey de Jerusalén, oyó que Josué había tomado Hai y la había consagrado al exterminio, que como había hecho a Jericó y a su rey, así había hecho a Hai y a su rey, y que los habitantes de Gabaón habían hecho paz con Israel y estaban en medio de ellos,
es.B: A Adonisedec, rey de Jerusalén, le llegó la noticia de que Josué había tomado Hai y la había consagrado al exterminio, y que había tratado a Hai y a su rey como había tratado a Jericó y a su rey. Supo también que los habitantes de Gabaón habían hecho la paz con Israel y ahora vivían entre ellos,
es.R: Adonisedec era el rey de Jerusalén. Oyó que Josué había tomado Hai y la había destruido por completo, como ciudad entregada {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Josué había hecho con Hai y su rey lo mismo que había hecho con Jericó y su rey. Adonisedec oyó también que la gente de Gabaón había hecho un tratado de paz con Israel y ahora vivía entre los israelitas.

decisions.choice: Adoni-Zedek: a king's name meaning "my lord is righteous" or "my lord is Zedek"
alternatives: my lord is Zedek (a god's name)
decisions.reason: The name joins the word for "lord" with the word for righteousness, which may also be the name of a god. It recalls Melchizedek, "king of righteousness", the king of Salem in Abraham's day (Genesis 14:18). Jerusalem was still a Jebusite city (15:63).

decisions.choice: devoted it to destruction: Ai and its people were given over to God completely
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for a "devoted thing" (Leviticus 27:28-29). Jericho was devoted to the LORD in this way (6:17, 21), and so was Ai (8:26), though at Ai the livestock and goods were kept as God allowed (8:2, 27).

decisions.choice: the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel: the treaty of chapter 9
decisions.reason: The Gibeonites tricked Israel into a treaty (9:3-15) and were allowed to live among Israel as its servants (9:26-27). "In their midst" means they now lived as part of Israel, protected by the oath.

decisions.choice: destroyed it completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 2:10 and Deuteronomy 2:34: Readable gives the sense of the term in plain words; Literal and Balanced keep "devote to destruction".

decisions.choice: two (Balanced) or four (Readable) sentences
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is one long clause of what the king heard, which runs into verse 2. Balanced and Readable divide it and repeat "he heard" before the second report.

decisions.choice: "Adoni-sedeki", "Yerusalemu"; "Hohamu", "Piramu", "Yarmuthi", "Yafia", "Lakishi", "Debiri", "Egloni" (verse 3)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua: "Yerusalemu" is the form used throughout the Swahili New Testament; the kings' and towns' names follow the Hebrew with the final vowel Swahili writes.

source.text: וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ מְאֹ֔ד כִּ֣י עִ֤יר גְּדוֹלָה֙ גִּבְע֔וֹן כְּאַחַ֖ת עָרֵ֣י הַמַּמְלָכָ֑ה וְכִ֨י הִ֤יא גְדוֹלָה֙ מִן־הָעַ֔י וְכָל־אֲנָשֶׁ֖יהָ גִּבֹּרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: and they feared greatly, for a city great [was] Gibeon, like one of [the] cities of the kingdom, and for it [was] greater than the Ai, and all its men [were] warriors.

en.L: that they feared greatly, because Gibeon [was] a great city, like one of the cities of the kingdom, and because it [was] greater than Ai, and all its men [were] mighty men.
en.B: he and his people were terrified, because Gibeon was an important city, like one of the royal cities; it was bigger than Ai, and its men were all warriors.
en.R: He and his people were terrified. Gibeon was a big city, as important as a city ruled by a king. It was bigger than Ai, and all its men were strong fighters.

sw.L: wakaogopa sana, kwa sababu Gibeoni [ulikuwa] mji mkubwa, kama mmoja wa miji ya kifalme, na kwa sababu [ulikuwa] mkubwa kuliko Ai, na watu wake wote [walikuwa] mashujaa.
sw.B: yeye na watu wake waliogopa sana, kwa sababu Gibeoni ulikuwa mji muhimu, kama mmoja wa miji ya kifalme; ulikuwa mkubwa kuliko Ai, na wanaume wake wote walikuwa wapiganaji.
sw.R: Yeye na watu wake waliogopa sana. Gibeoni ulikuwa mji mkubwa, wenye umuhimu kama mji unaotawaliwa na mfalme. Ulikuwa mkubwa kuliko Ai, na wanaume wake wote walikuwa wapiganaji hodari.

es.L: temieron mucho, porque Gabaón [era] una ciudad grande, como una de las ciudades del reino, y porque [era] mayor que Hai, y todos sus hombres [eran] guerreros.
es.B: él y su pueblo tuvieron mucho miedo, porque Gabaón era una ciudad importante, como una de las ciudades reales; era más grande que Hai, y todos sus hombres eran guerreros.
es.R: Él y su pueblo tuvieron mucho miedo. Gabaón era una ciudad grande, tan importante como una ciudad gobernada por un rey. Era más grande que Hai, y todos sus hombres eran guerreros fuertes.

decisions.choice: they feared: the king and his people
decisions.reason: The verb is plural although verse 1 names only the king. The fear belongs to Adoni-Zedek and the people of Jerusalem together, as Rahab said all Canaan feared Israel (2:9-11).

decisions.choice: like one of the royal cities: a city as strong as those that had their own king
decisions.reason: Gibeon is not said to have had a king; its elders speak for it (9:11). It was still as large and strong as a city that was the seat of a king, so its going over to Israel was a serious loss to the kings of the region.

decisions.choice: mighty men: warriors, men able in battle
decisions.reason: The word describes strong fighting men (6:2). Gibeon had not made peace because it was weak.

decisions.choice: he and his people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are, because the sentence began with the king alone (m1).

decisions.choice: as important as a city ruled by a king
decisions.reason: Readable explains "royal cities" in plain words.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אֲדֹנִי־צֶ֜דֶק מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֶל־הוֹהָ֣ם מֶֽלֶךְ־חֶ֠בְרוֹן וְאֶל־פִּרְאָ֨ם מֶֽלֶךְ־יַרְמ֜וּת וְאֶל־יָפִ֧יעַ מֶֽלֶךְ־לָכִ֛ישׁ וְאֶל־דְּבִ֥יר מֶֽלֶךְ־עֶגְל֖וֹן לֵאמֹֽר׃

en.L: And Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron and to Piram king of Jarmuth and to Japhia king of Lachish and to Debir king of Eglon, saying,

en.R: So Adoni-Zedek sent messengers to four other kings: Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon. He told them,

sw.L: Adoni-sedeki mfalme wa Yerusalemu akatuma kwa Hohamu mfalme wa Hebroni, na kwa Piramu mfalme wa Yarmuthi, na kwa Yafia mfalme wa Lakishi, na kwa Debiri mfalme wa Egloni, akisema,
sw.B: Basi Adoni-sedeki mfalme wa Yerusalemu alituma ujumbe huu kwa Hohamu mfalme wa Hebroni, Piramu mfalme wa Yarmuthi, Yafia mfalme wa Lakishi na Debiri mfalme wa Egloni:
sw.R: Basi Adoni-sedeki aliwatuma wajumbe kwa wafalme wengine wanne: Hohamu mfalme wa Hebroni, Piramu mfalme wa Yarmuthi, Yafia mfalme wa Lakishi, na Debiri mfalme wa Egloni. Aliwaambia,

es.L: Y Adonisedec, rey de Jerusalén, envió a Hoham, rey de Hebrón, y a Piram, rey de Jarmut, y a Jafía, rey de Laquis, y a Debir, rey de Eglón, diciendo:
es.B: Así que Adonisedec, rey de Jerusalén, envió este mensaje a Hoham, rey de Hebrón, a Piram, rey de Jarmut, a Jafía, rey de Laquis, y a Debir, rey de Eglón:
es.R: Así que Adonisedec envió mensajeros a otros cuatro reyes: Hoham, rey de Hebrón; Piram, rey de Jarmut; Jafía, rey de Laquis; y Debir, rey de Eglón. Les dijo:

decisions.choice: Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, Eglon: cities south and southwest of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Hebron lies in the hills to the south; Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon lie in the low hills to the southwest. Here Debir is the name of the king of Eglon, not the town of Debir taken in verses 38-39.

decisions.choice: sent messengers to four other kings
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "sent to"; Readable says how a king sent word and counts the kings for the reader.

decisions.choice: "Adonisedec", "Hoham", "Piram", "Jarmut", "Jafía", "Laquis", "Debir", "Eglón"
decisions.reason: The names take their usual Spanish forms, with "j" for the Hebrew h-sound as in "Sijón" in Deuteronomy. They are recorded here so that the later lists of kings in chapter 12 use the same forms.

source.text: עֲלֽוּ־אֵלַ֣י וְעִזְרֻ֔נִי וְנַכֶּ֖ה אֶת־גִּבְע֑וֹן כִּֽי־הִשְׁלִ֥ימָה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: "Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel."
en.B: "Come up and help me, and let us attack Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."
en.R: "Come and help me attack Gibeon, because its people have made peace with Joshua and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

sw.L: "Pandeni kwangu mnisaidie, tuupige Gibeoni, kwa sababu umefanya amani na Yoshua na wana wa Israeli."
sw.B: "Njooni mnisaidie, tuushambulie Gibeoni, kwa sababu umefanya amani na Yoshua na Waisraeli."
sw.R: "Njooni mnisaidie kuushambulia Gibeoni, kwa sababu watu wake wamefanya amani na Yoshua na Waisraeli."

es.L: «{{plural_you:Suban|Subid}} a mí y {{plural_you:ayúdenme|ayudadme}}, y ataquemos a Gabaón, porque ha hecho paz con Josué y con los hijos de Israel».
es.B: «{{plural_you:Suban|Subid}} y {{plural_you:ayúdenme|ayudadme}}, y ataquemos a Gabaón, porque ha hecho la paz con Josué y con los israelitas».
es.R: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} a ayudarme a atacar a Gabaón, porque su gente ha hecho la paz con Josué y con los israelitas».

decisions.choice: strike: attack in battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or hit and is used for attacking and defeating an enemy (verses 10, 20).

decisions.choice: it has made peace: the city stands for its people
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine singular, agreeing with the city. By making peace with Israel, Gibeon had become an enemy of the kings around it.

decisions.choice: its people
decisions.reason: Readable says that the people of the city made the treaty.

source.text: וַיֵּאָסְפ֨וּ וַֽיַּעֲל֜וּ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת׀מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֗י מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם מֶֽלֶךְ־חֶבְר֤וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־יַרְמוּת֙ מֶֽלֶךְ־לָכִ֣ישׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־עֶגְל֔וֹן הֵ֖ם וְכָל־מַֽחֲנֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ עַל־גִּבְע֔וֹן וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עָלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered and went up five kings of the Amorite, king of Jerusalem, king of Hebron, king of Jarmuth, king of Lachish, king of Eglon, they and all their camps, and encamped against Gibeon and fought against it.

en.L: And the five kings of the Amorites gathered and went up, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon, they and all their camps, and they camped against Gibeon and made war against it.
en.B: Then the five Amorite kings, the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon, joined forces. They went up with all their armies, camped against Gibeon and attacked it.
en.R: So the five Amorite kings joined together: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon. They marched out with all their armies. They set up camp around Gibeon and attacked it.

sw.L: Wafalme watano wa Waamori wakakusanyika, wakapanda, mfalme wa Yerusalemu, mfalme wa Hebroni, mfalme wa Yarmuthi, mfalme wa Lakishi, mfalme wa Egloni, wao na kambi zao zote, wakapiga kambi kuukabili Gibeoni, wakapigana nao.
sw.B: Ndipo wale wafalme watano wa Waamori, wafalme wa Yerusalemu, Hebroni, Yarmuthi, Lakishi na Egloni, waliunganisha majeshi yao. Walipanda na majeshi yao yote, wakapiga kambi kuukabili Gibeoni, wakaushambulia.
sw.R: Basi wale wafalme watano wa Waamori waliungana: wafalme wa Yerusalemu, Hebroni, Yarmuthi, Lakishi na Egloni. Walitoka na majeshi yao yote. Wakapiga kambi kuuzunguka Gibeoni, wakaushambulia.

es.L: Y se reunieron y subieron los cinco reyes de los amorreos, el rey de Jerusalén, el rey de Hebrón, el rey de Jarmut, el rey de Laquis, el rey de Eglón, ellos y todos sus campamentos, y acamparon contra Gabaón y la combatieron.
es.B: Entonces los cinco reyes amorreos, los reyes de Jerusalén, Hebrón, Jarmut, Laquis y Eglón, unieron sus fuerzas. Subieron con todos sus ejércitos, acamparon frente a Gabaón y la atacaron.
es.R: Así que los cinco reyes amorreos se unieron: los reyes de Jerusalén, Hebrón, Jarmut, Laquis y Eglón. Salieron con todos sus ejércitos. Acamparon alrededor de Gabaón y la atacaron.

decisions.choice: the Amorites: the peoples of the hill country
decisions.reason: "Amorite" is used for the peoples of the hill country of Canaan in general (verse 6; Deuteronomy 1:7, 19-20). The Gibeonites themselves are called Hivites (9:7).

decisions.choice: all their camps: their armies, the forces in the field
decisions.reason: A "camp" is an army on the march or encamped; the plural means the separate forces of the five kings.

decisions.choice: armies
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "camps"; Balanced and Readable name what the camps were.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ גִבְע֨וֹן אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ הַגִּלְגָּ֣לָה לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל־תֶּ֥רֶף יָדֶ֖יךָ מֵֽעֲבָדֶ֑יךָ עֲלֵ֧ה אֵלֵ֣ינוּ מְהֵרָ֗ה וְהוֹשִׁ֤יעָה לָּ֨נוּ֙ וְעָזְרֵ֔נוּ כִּ֚י נִקְבְּצ֣וּ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ כָּל־מַלְכֵ֥י הָאֱמֹרִ֖י יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent [the] men of Gibeon to Joshua to the camp at Gilgal, saying, Do not let drop your hands from your slaves; come up to us quickly and save us and help us, for have gathered against us all [the] kings of the Amorite dwelling [in] the hill country.

en.L: And the men of Gibeon sent to Joshua, to the camp at Gilgal, saying, "Do not let your hands drop from your slaves. Come up to us quickly, and save us and help us, because all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us."
en.B: The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal: "Do not abandon your servants! Come up to us quickly. Rescue us and help us, because all the Amorite kings of the hill country have joined forces against us."
en.R: The men of Gibeon sent a message to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal. They said, "Do not leave us, your servants, without help! Come quickly and save us. All the Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together to attack us."

sw.L: Watu wa Gibeoni wakatuma kwa Yoshua, kambini huko Gilgali, wakisema, "Usiilegeze mikono yako kwa watumwa wako. Panda kwetu upesi, utuokoe na kutusaidia, kwa sababu wafalme wote wa Waamori wanaokaa katika nchi ya milima wamekusanyika juu yetu."
sw.B: Watu wa Gibeoni walituma ujumbe kwa Yoshua kambini huko Gilgali: "Usiwaache watumishi wako! Panda kwetu upesi. Utuokoe na kutusaidia, kwa sababu wafalme wote wa Waamori wa nchi ya milima wameunganisha majeshi yao dhidi yetu."
sw.R: Watu wa Gibeoni walimtumia Yoshua ujumbe kambini huko Gilgali. Walisema, "Usituache sisi watumishi wako bila msaada! Njoo upesi utuokoe. Wafalme wote wa Waamori kutoka nchi ya vilima wameungana kutushambulia."

es.L: Y los hombres de Gabaón enviaron a Josué, al campamento en Gilgal, diciendo: «No retires tus manos de tus esclavos. Sube a nosotros pronto, y sálvanos y ayúdanos, porque se han reunido contra nosotros todos los reyes de los amorreos que habitan en la región montañosa».
es.B: Los hombres de Gabaón le mandaron decir a Josué, al campamento de Gilgal: «¡No abandones a tus siervos! Sube pronto a donde estamos. Rescátanos y ayúdanos, porque todos los reyes amorreos de la región montañosa se han unido contra nosotros».
es.R: Los hombres de Gabaón le enviaron un mensaje a Josué, al campamento de Gilgal. Le dijeron: «¡No nos dejes sin ayuda a nosotros, tus siervos! Ven pronto y sálvanos. Todos los reyes amorreos de la región montañosa se han unido para atacarnos».

decisions.choice: do not let your hands drop from: do not abandon, do not withdraw your support
decisions.reason: To let the hands drop is to let go, to stop holding on to someone or something (Deuteronomy 31:6, 8, "he will not let you go").

decisions.choice: your slaves: the Gibeonites as Israel's bound servants under the treaty
decisions.reason: They had called themselves Joshua's servants (9:8, 11), and Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for Israel (9:23, 27). Now they call on their master to protect them.

decisions.choice: the hill country: the central highlands
decisions.reason: The ridge of hills running north and south through the land, where Jerusalem, Hebron and Gibeon stand. Gilgal lay far below, near the Jordan (4:19).

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal), servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for this word: Literal keeps its hard edge; Balanced and Readable say "servants". Their position is described in m2.

decisions.choice: Do not abandon (Balanced) / Do not leave us ... without help (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m1).

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַל יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ מִן־הַגִּלְגָּ֗ל ה֚וּא וְכָל־עַ֤ם הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל גִּבּוֹרֵ֥י הֶחָֽיִל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went up Joshua from the Gilgal, he and all [the] people of the war with him and all [the] mighty men of the strength.

en.L: And Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valor.
en.B: So Joshua went up from Gilgal with his whole army, including all his best fighting men.
en.R: So Joshua marched up from Gilgal with his whole army, including all his best soldiers.

sw.L: Yoshua akapanda kutoka Gilgali, yeye na watu wote wa vita pamoja naye, na mashujaa wote wenye nguvu.
sw.B: Basi Yoshua alipanda kutoka Gilgali pamoja na jeshi lake lote, wakiwemo wapiganaji wake hodari wote.
sw.R: Basi Yoshua alipanda kutoka Gilgali pamoja na jeshi lake lote, wakiwemo askari wake hodari wote.

es.L: Y subió Josué de Gilgal, él y toda la gente de guerra con él, y todos los valientes guerreros.
es.B: Así que Josué subió de Gilgal con todo su ejército, incluidos todos sus mejores guerreros.
es.R: Así que Josué subió desde Gilgal con todo su ejército, incluidos sus mejores soldados.

decisions.choice: and all the mighty men of valor: the best warriors within the army
alternatives: a second name for the whole army
decisions.reason: The second phrase may single out the strongest fighters within the whole fighting force, as in 8:3, or it may be a second name for the same army.

decisions.choice: went up: the long climb from the Jordan valley into the hills
decisions.reason: Gilgal lay near Jericho in the Jordan valley, far below Gibeon in the hills; the march meant a steep climb over many miles.

decisions.choice: his whole army
decisions.reason: "All the people of war" means all the fighting men; Balanced and Readable say "army".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אַל־תִּירָ֣א מֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י בְיָדְךָ֖ נְתַתִּ֑ים לֹֽא־יַעֲמֹ֥ד אִ֛ישׁ מֵהֶ֖ם בְּפָנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Joshua, Do not fear them, for into your hand I have given them; not will stand a man of them before you.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not fear them, for I have given them into your hand. Not a man of them will stand before you."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. I have handed them over to you. Not one of them will be able to stand against you."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. I have already handed them over to you. Not one of them will be able to stop you."

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Yoshua, "Usiwaogope, kwa maana nimewatia mkononi mwako; hakuna mtu kati yao atakayesimama mbele yako."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua, "Usiwaogope. Nimewatia mikononi mwako. Hakuna hata mmoja wao atakayeweza kusimama dhidi yako."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua, "Usiwaogope. Tayari nimewatia mikononi mwako. Hakuna hata mmoja wao atakayeweza kukuzuia."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Josué: «No les temas, porque los he entregado en tu mano. Ni un hombre de ellos se mantendrá en pie delante de ti».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Josué: «No les tengas miedo. Te los he entregado. Ninguno de ellos podrá hacerte frente».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Josué: «No les tengas miedo. Ya te los he entregado. Ninguno de ellos podrá detenerte».

decisions.choice: I have given them: the victory is as good as done
decisions.reason: God speaks of the battle as already decided, before it begins, as at Jericho (6:2) and Ai (8:1).

decisions.choice: into your hand: into your power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control.

decisions.choice: not a man of them will stand before you: the promise of 1:5
decisions.reason: God promised Joshua that no one would be able to stand before him all his life (1:5; Deuteronomy 7:24).

decisions.choice: already
decisions.reason: Readable adds "already" to show that God speaks of the victory as settled (m1).

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ פִּתְאֹ֑ם כָּל־הַלַּ֕יְלָה עָלָ֖ה מִן־הַגִּלְגָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And came to them Joshua suddenly; all the night he had gone up from the Gilgal.

en.L: And Joshua came upon them suddenly; all night he had gone up from Gilgal.
en.B: Joshua marched all night from Gilgal and came upon them by surprise.
en.R: Joshua and his army marched all night from Gilgal and attacked them by surprise.

sw.L: Yoshua akawajia ghafla; usiku kucha alikuwa amepanda kutoka Gilgali.
sw.B: Yoshua alitembea usiku kucha kutoka Gilgali, akawashambulia ghafla.
sw.R: Yoshua na jeshi lake walitembea usiku kucha kutoka Gilgali, wakawashambulia ghafla.

es.L: Y Josué cayó sobre ellos de repente; toda la noche había subido desde Gilgal.
es.B: Josué marchó toda la noche desde Gilgal y cayó sobre ellos por sorpresa.
es.R: Josué y su ejército marcharon toda la noche desde Gilgal y los atacaron por sorpresa.

decisions.choice: all night he had gone up: the night march explains the surprise
decisions.reason: The second clause gives the background of the first: because Joshua climbed through the night, he reached the enemy before they expected him.

decisions.choice: marched all night ... and came upon them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tell the night march first, in the order things happened.

decisions.choice: and his army ... attacked them
decisions.reason: Readable says that the army went with Joshua (verse 7) and that "came upon them" means he attacked.

source.text: וַיְהֻמֵּ֤ם יְהוָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּכֵּ֥ם מַכָּֽה־גְדוֹלָ֖ה בְּגִבְע֑וֹן וַֽיִּרְדְּפֵ֗ם דֶּ֚רֶךְ מַעֲלֵ֣ה בֵית־חוֹרֹ֔ן וַיַּכֵּ֥ם עַד־עֲזֵקָ֖ה וְעַד־מַקֵּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And threw into panic them Yahweh before Israel, and struck them [a] striking great at Gibeon, and pursued them [by the] way of [the] ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and as far as Makkedah.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} threw them into panic before Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck them [with] a great striking at Gibeon, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pursued them by the way of the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and as far as Makkedah.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} threw them into panic before Israel and struck them with a great defeat at Gibeon. He chased them along the road that climbs to Beth-horon and struck them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the Amorites panic when they faced Israel, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck them down at Gibeon in a great defeat. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} chased them along the road up to Beth-horon and struck them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawafadhaisha mbele ya Israeli, akawapiga pigo kuu huko Gibeoni, akawafuatia kwa njia ya kupandia Beth-horoni, akawapiga hadi Azeka na hadi Makeda.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatia hofu kuu mbele ya Israeli, akawashinda kabisa huko Gibeoni. Aliwafukuza kwa njia inayopanda kwenda Beth-horoni, akawapiga njia yote hadi Azeka na Makeda.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatia Waamori hofu kuu walipokutana na Israeli, akawashinda kabisa huko Gibeoni. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwafukuza kwa njia inayopanda kwenda Beth-horoni, akawaua njia yote hadi Azeka na Makeda.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los llenó de pánico delante de Israel, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los hirió con gran mortandad en Gabaón, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los persiguió por el camino de la subida de Bet-jorón, y los hirió hasta Azeca y hasta Maceda.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los llenó de pánico delante de Israel y los derrotó con una gran matanza en Gabaón. Los persiguió por el camino que sube a Bet-jorón y los fue abatiendo hasta Azeca y Maceda.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo que los amorreos se llenaran de pánico cuando se enfrentaron a Israel, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los derrotó en Gabaón con una gran matanza. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los persiguió por el camino que sube a Bet-jorón y los fue abatiendo hasta Azeca y Maceda.

decisions.choice: threw into panic: the terror and confusion God sends on an enemy
decisions.reason: The verb is used when God throws an army into confusion so that it breaks and runs (Exodus 14:24; Judges 4:15; 1 Samuel 7:10).

decisions.choice: he struck ... pursued ... struck: the LORD is the subject, acting through Israel's army
alternatives: Israel (or Joshua) struck them and pursued them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name a new subject after "the LORD", so the verbs that follow are his. The chapter says the LORD fought for Israel (verses 14, 42), while Israel's soldiers did the fighting with the sword (verse 11). The verbs may also be read with Joshua or Israel as their subject.

decisions.choice: the ascent of Beth-horon, Azekah, Makkedah: the line of the flight
decisions.reason: The road ran west from Gibeon up to Beth-horon and down from the hills (verse 11). Azekah and Makkedah lie in the low hills to the southwest.

decisions.choice: the Amorites ... when they faced Israel
decisions.reason: Readable names the enemy and explains "before Israel". It repeats "the LORD" to show who chased them (m2).

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י בְּנֻסָ֣ם׀מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הֵ֞ם בְּמוֹרַ֤ד בֵּית־חוֹרֹן֙ וַֽיהוָ֡ה הִשְׁלִ֣יךְ עֲלֵיהֶם֩ אֲבָנִ֨ים גְּדֹל֧וֹת מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם עַד־עֲזֵקָ֖ה וַיָּמֻ֑תוּ רַבִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־מֵ֨תוּ֙ בְּאַבְנֵ֣י הַבָּרָ֔ד מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרְג֛וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּחָֽרֶב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as they fled from before Israel, they [were] on [the] descent of Beth-horon, and Yahweh threw on them stones great from the heavens as far as Azekah, and they died; more [were those] who died by [the] stones of the hail than [those] whom killed [the] sons of Israel with the sword.

en.L: And it happened, as they fled before Israel, [while] they [were] on the descent of Beth-horon, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} threw large stones on them from the heavens as far as Azekah, and they died. More [were] those who died by the stones of the hail than those whom the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel killed with the sword.
en.B: As they fled before Israel down the slope from Beth-horon, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hurled huge stones on them from the sky all the way to Azekah, and they died. More of them died from the hailstones than the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} killed with the sword.
en.R: As the Amorites ran from Israel down the road from Beth-horon, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} threw huge hailstones down on them from the sky all the way to Azekah. More of them were killed by the hail than by the swords of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

sw.L: Ikawa walipokuwa wakikimbia mbele ya Israeli, [walipokuwa] kwenye mteremko wa Beth-horoni, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatupia mawe makubwa kutoka mbinguni hadi Azeka, wakafa. Waliokufa kwa mawe ya mvua ya mawe walikuwa wengi kuliko wale ambao wana wa Israeli waliwaua kwa upanga.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakikimbia mbele ya Israeli kwenye mteremko wa Beth-horoni, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatupia mawe makubwa kutoka angani njia yote hadi Azeka, nao wakafa. Waliokufa kwa mvua ya mawe walikuwa wengi kuliko wale ambao Waisraeli waliwaua kwa upanga.
sw.R: Waamori walipokuwa wakiwakimbia Israeli wakiteremka kutoka Beth-horoni, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatupia mawe makubwa ya mvua kutoka angani njia yote hadi Azeka. Wengi wao waliuawa kwa mvua hiyo ya mawe kuliko waliouawa kwa panga za Waisraeli.

es.L: Y sucedió que, mientras huían delante de Israel, [estando] en la bajada de Bet-jorón, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} arrojó sobre ellos grandes piedras desde el cielo hasta Azeca, y murieron. Más [fueron] los que murieron por las piedras del granizo que los que mataron los hijos de Israel a espada.
es.B: Mientras huían ante Israel por la bajada de Bet-jorón, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lanzó sobre ellos enormes piedras desde el cielo hasta Azeca, y murieron. Fueron más los que murieron por el granizo que los que mataron a espada los israelitas.
es.R: Mientras los amorreos huían de Israel por el camino que baja de Bet-jorón, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les lanzó desde el cielo enormes piedras de granizo, hasta Azeca. El granizo mató a más de ellos que las espadas de los israelitas.

decisions.choice: large stones from the heavens: hailstones
decisions.reason: The same stones are called "stones of the hail" in the second half of the verse. God used hail against Egypt too (Exodus 9:23-25), and hail is among his weapons in Job 38:22-23 and Psalm 18:13-14.

decisions.choice: more died by the hail than by the sword: the victory was the LORD's
decisions.reason: The count shows that God, more than Israel's army, won the battle, as verse 14 says: the LORD fought for Israel.

decisions.choice: hailstones
decisions.reason: Readable says at once what the stones were (m1), and names the Amorites as those who fled.

source.text: אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה בְּי֗וֹם תֵּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀לְעֵינֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שֶׁ֚מֶשׁ בְּגִבְע֣וֹן דּ֔וֹם וְיָרֵ֖חַ בְּעֵ֥מֶק אַיָּלֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Then spoke Joshua to Yahweh on [the] day [of] giving Yahweh the Amorite before [the] sons of Israel, and he said in [the] eyes of Israel, Sun, at Gibeon be still, and moon, in [the] valley of Aijalon.

en.L: Then Joshua spoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the Amorites over before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, \q and he said in the sight of Israel, \q "Sun, at Gibeon be still, \q and moon, in the valley of Aijalon."
en.B: On the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the Amorites up to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, Joshua spoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q In full view of Israel he said, \q "Sun, stand still at Gibeon, \q and moon, in the valley of Aijalon!"
en.R: On the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} victory over the Amorites, Joshua spoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q With all Israel listening, he said, \q "Sun, stand still at Gibeon! \q Moon, stand still in the valley of Aijalon!"

sw.L: Ndipo Yoshua akasema na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} siku ile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipowatoa Waamori mbele ya wana wa Israeli, \q akasema machoni pa Israeli, \q "Jua, tulia juu ya Gibeoni, \q nawe mwezi, katika bonde la Ayaloni."
sw.B: Siku ile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipowatia Waamori mikononi mwa Waisraeli, Yoshua alisema na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Mbele ya Israeli wote alisema, \q "Jua, simama kimya juu ya Gibeoni, \q nawe mwezi, juu ya bonde la Ayaloni!"
sw.R: Siku ile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipowapa Waisraeli ushindi juu ya Waamori, Yoshua alisema na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Israeli wote wakisikia, alisema, \q "Jua, simama kimya juu ya Gibeoni! \q Mwezi, simama kimya juu ya bonde la Ayaloni!"

es.L: Entonces Josué habló {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} el día en que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entregó a los amorreos delante de los hijos de Israel, \q y dijo a la vista de Israel: \q «Sol, en Gabaón quédate quieto, \q y luna, en el valle de Ajalón».
es.B: El día en que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entregó a los amorreos en manos de los israelitas, Josué habló {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q A la vista de Israel dijo: \q «Sol, quédate inmóvil sobre Gabaón, \q y tú, luna, sobre el valle de Ajalón».
es.R: El día en que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les dio a los israelitas la victoria sobre los amorreos, Josué habló {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q Mientras todo Israel escuchaba, dijo: \q «¡Sol, no te muevas de encima de Gabaón! \q ¡Luna, quédate quieta sobre el valle de Ajalón!».

decisions.choice: be still: stop, stay where you are
decisions.reason: The verb means to be still or silent, to stop moving or stop acting (1 Samuel 14:9, "wait"; Psalm 4:5). Verse 13 takes it up with a second verb, "stood", so here it means that the sun should stop. Because the same verb can mean "be silent", some read it as a call for the sun to stop shining; see the note at verse 13.

decisions.choice: spoke to the LORD ... said in the sight of Israel: a prayer spoken as a command to sun and moon
decisions.reason: Joshua speaks to the LORD, yet his words are addressed to the sun and the moon, in front of all Israel. Verse 14 treats them as a request that the LORD heard: "the LORD listened to the voice of a man".

decisions.choice: at Gibeon ... in the valley of Aijalon: the sun to the east, the moon to the west
decisions.reason: Gibeon stands on the hills; the valley of Aijalon opens to the west of it, along the route of the flight (verses 10-11). The places named for the sun and the moon may say where Joshua saw them in the sky.

decisions.choice: the saying is a short poem
decisions.reason: The words to the sun and the moon, and the lines that follow in verse 13, are set in two matching lines each, as Hebrew poetry is. Verse 13 says they were written in the Book of Jashar.

decisions.choice: On the day the LORD handed the Amorites over ... Joshua spoke
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the time first. Readable says "gave ... victory over" for "gave ... before", and "with all Israel listening" for "in the sight of Israel".

decisions.choice: "quédate quieto" (Literal); "quédate inmóvil" (Balanced); "no te muevas" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be still or silent, to stop (m1). Spanish uses plain words for staying still and keeps the Hebrew order at Literal ("Sun, at Gibeon be still"), rather than the familiar wording of older Spanish versions.

source.text: וַיִּדֹּ֨ם הַשֶּׁ֜מֶשׁ וְיָרֵ֣חַ עָמָ֗ד עַד־יִקֹּ֥ם גּוֹי֙ אֹֽיְבָ֔יו הֲלֹא־הִ֥יא כְתוּבָ֖ה עַל־סֵ֣פֶר הַיָּשָׁ֑ר וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְלֹא־אָ֥ץ לָב֖וֹא כְּי֥וֹם תָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And was still the sun, and [the] moon stood, until took vengeance [the] nation [on] its enemies. [Is] it not written on [the] scroll of the Jashar? And stood the sun in [the] half of the heavens, and not hastened to go about a day complete.

en.L: And the sun was still, and the moon stood, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies. \q Is it not written in the Book of Jashar? \q And the sun stood in the middle of the heavens \q and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.
en.B: So the sun stood still, and the moon halted, until the nation had taken vengeance on its enemies. \q Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? \q The sun stopped in the middle of the sky \q and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.
en.R: So the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the people of Israel had paid back their enemies. \q This is written in the Book of Jashar, a book of old songs. \q The sun stopped in the middle of the sky. \q It waited about a whole day before it went down.

sw.L: Jua likatulia, na mwezi ukasimama, mpaka taifa lilipojilipiza kisasi juu ya adui zake. \q Je, si [haya] yameandikwa katika Kitabu cha Yashari? \q Jua likasimama katikati ya mbingu, \q wala halikufanya haraka kutua kama siku nzima.
sw.B: Basi jua lilisimama kimya, na mwezi ukasimama, mpaka taifa lilipomaliza kujilipiza kisasi juu ya adui zake. \q Je, haya hayakuandikwa katika Kitabu cha Yashari? \q Jua lilisimama katikati ya anga, \q wala halikuharakisha kutua kwa muda wa kama siku nzima.
sw.R: Basi jua lilisimama kimya, na mwezi ukasimama, mpaka watu wa Israeli walipowalipa adui zao. \q Habari hii imeandikwa katika Kitabu cha Yashari, kitabu cha nyimbo za zamani. \q Jua lilisimama katikati ya anga. \q Lilingoja kama siku nzima kabla ya kutua.

es.L: Y quieto quedó el sol, y la luna se mantuvo, hasta que la nación tomó venganza de sus enemigos. \q ¿Acaso no está escrito en el libro de Jaser? \q Y el sol permaneció en medio del cielo \q y no tuvo prisa por ocultarse durante casi un día completo.
es.B: Así el sol se quedó inmóvil y la luna se paró, hasta que la nación hizo pagar a sus enemigos. \q ¿Acaso no lo cuenta el libro de Jaser? \q El sol se quedó en medio del cielo \q y tardó casi un día entero en ponerse.
es.R: Así que el sol se quedó quieto y la luna se paró, hasta que el pueblo de Israel les dio su merecido a sus enemigos. \q Esto está escrito en el libro de Jaser, un libro de cantos antiguos. \q El sol se quedó parado en medio del cielo. \q Esperó casi un día entero antes de ponerse.

decisions.choice: what is described: daylight held on until the battle was won; how it happened is not said
alternatives: the sun's course was halted and the day made longer
the sun was silent: its heat or light was withheld
the sun and moon stood in positions read as a sign of victory
a poetic picture of a day of complete victory
decisions.reason: The poem says the sun "was still" and the moon "stood" until Israel had defeated its enemies. The prose that follows says the sun stood in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set for about a whole day, and verse 14 says no day was like it, because the LORD listened to a man. The text's own weight falls on God hearing Joshua and fighting for Israel; it does not explain how the day was lengthened. Readers have understood it in several ways: that the sun's course was truly halted and the day made longer; that "be still" means "be silent", so that the sun's heat or light was held back, perhaps by the storm of verse 11; that the sun and moon were seen in positions taken as a sign of victory; or that the poem's bold picture means a victory so complete that the day seemed to stretch out. The text itself does not decide between these.

Both quotations are poems about Israel's battles and heroes, so it seems to have been a collection of songs. No copy of it has survived. The question "Is it not written...?" points the reader to a source they could check.

es.B: Entonces Josué dijo: «{{plural_you:Abran|Abrid}} la boca de la cueva y {{plural_you:tráiganme|traedme}} a esos cinco reyes».
es.R: Entonces Josué dijo: «{{plural_you:Abran|Abrid}} la cueva y {{plural_you:tráiganme|traedme}} a los cinco reyes».

decisions.choice: "from the cave" not repeated
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the cave twice; Balanced and Readable say it once.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עֲשׂוּ כֵ֔ן וַיֹּצִ֣יאוּ אֵלָ֗יו אֶת־חֲמֵ֛שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה מִן־הַמְּעָרָ֑ה אֵ֣ת׀מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֶת־מֶ֤לֶךְ חֶבְרוֹן֙ אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ יַרְמ֔וּת אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ לָכִ֖ישׁ אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ עֶגְלֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they did so, and brought out to him five the kings the these from the cave: king of Jerusalem, king of Hebron, king of Jarmuth, king of Lachish, king of Eglon.

en.L: And they did so, and they brought out to him these five kings from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon.
en.B: They did so. They brought the five kings out of the cave to him: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon.
en.R: So they brought the five kings out of the cave to Joshua. They were the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon.

sw.L: Wakafanya hivyo, wakamtolea wafalme hao watano kutoka pangoni: mfalme wa Yerusalemu, mfalme wa Hebroni, mfalme wa Yarmuthi, mfalme wa Lakishi, mfalme wa Egloni.
sw.B: Wakafanya hivyo. Waliwatoa pangoni wale wafalme watano, wakamletea: wafalme wa Yerusalemu, Hebroni, Yarmuthi, Lakishi na Egloni.
sw.R: Basi waliwatoa wale wafalme watano pangoni, wakawaleta kwa Yoshua. Walikuwa wafalme wa Yerusalemu, Hebroni, Yarmuthi, Lakishi na Egloni.

es.L: Y así lo hicieron, y le sacaron de la cueva a estos cinco reyes: el rey de Jerusalén, el rey de Hebrón, el rey de Jarmut, el rey de Laquis, el rey de Eglón.
es.B: Así lo hicieron. Le sacaron de la cueva a los cinco reyes: los reyes de Jerusalén, Hebrón, Jarmut, Laquis y Eglón.
es.R: Así que sacaron de la cueva a los cinco reyes y se los llevaron a Josué. Eran los reyes de Jerusalén, Hebrón, Jarmut, Laquis y Eglón.

decisions.choice: the king of Jerusalem ... of Eglon: the five kings of verses 3 and 5
decisions.reason: The list repeats the five cities of verse 5, so that each king is named as he is brought out.

decisions.choice: to Joshua
decisions.reason: Readable names Joshua for "him".

source.text: וַ֠יְהִי כְּֽהוֹצִיאָ֞ם אֶת־הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵלֶּה֮ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֒ וַיִּקְרָ֨א יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶל־כָּל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אֶל־קְצִינֵ֞י אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ הֶהָלְכ֣וּא אִתּ֔וֹ קִרְב֗וּ שִׂ֚ימוּ אֶת־רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם עַֽל־צַוְּארֵ֖י הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַֽיִּקְרְב֔וּ וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ אֶת־רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־צַוְּארֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when they brought out the kings the these to Joshua, and called Joshua to every man of Israel, and said to [the] commanders of [the] men of the war who had gone with him, Come near; put your feet on [the] necks of the kings the these. And they came near and put their feet on their necks.

en.L: And it happened, when they had brought out these kings to Joshua, that Joshua called for every man of Israel, and he said to the commanders of the men of war who had gone with him, "Come near; put your feet on the necks of these kings." And they came near and put their feet on their necks.
en.B: When they had brought these kings out to Joshua, he called for all the men of Israel. He told the commanders of the soldiers who had gone with him, "Come forward and put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came forward and placed their feet on their necks.
en.R: When the kings were brought to Joshua, he called all the men of Israel together. He said to the army commanders who had gone with him, "Come here. Put your feet on the necks of these kings." The commanders came forward and put their feet on the kings' necks.

sw.L: Ikawa walipowaleta wafalme hao kwa Yoshua, Yoshua akawaita watu wote wa Israeli, akawaambia wakuu wa watu wa vita waliokwenda pamoja naye, "Njooni karibu, wekeni miguu yenu juu ya shingo za wafalme hawa." Wakakaribia, wakaweka miguu yao juu ya shingo zao.
sw.B: Walipowaleta wafalme hao kwa Yoshua, aliwaita wanaume wote wa Israeli. Akawaambia makamanda wa askari waliokwenda pamoja naye, "Njooni mweke miguu yenu juu ya shingo za wafalme hawa." Basi wakaja, wakaweka miguu yao juu ya shingo zao.
sw.R: Wafalme hao walipoletwa kwa Yoshua, aliwaita wanaume wote wa Israeli pamoja. Akawaambia makamanda wa jeshi waliokwenda pamoja naye, "Njooni hapa. Wekeni miguu yenu juu ya shingo za wafalme hawa." Makamanda walikuja, wakaweka miguu yao juu ya shingo za wafalme.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando sacaron a estos reyes ante Josué, Josué llamó a todos los hombres de Israel, y dijo a los jefes de los hombres de guerra que habían ido con él: «{{plural_you:Acérquense|Acercaos}}; {{plural_you:pongan sus pies|poned vuestros pies}} sobre el cuello de estos reyes». Y ellos se acercaron y pusieron sus pies sobre sus cuellos.
es.B: Cuando le llevaron estos reyes a Josué, él llamó a todos los hombres de Israel. Dijo a los jefes de los soldados que habían ido con él: «{{plural_you:Acérquense|Acercaos}} y {{plural_you:pongan|poned}} el pie sobre el cuello de estos reyes». Ellos se acercaron y les pusieron el pie sobre el cuello.
es.R: Cuando le llevaron los reyes a Josué, él reunió a todos los hombres de Israel. Dijo a los jefes del ejército que habían ido con él: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} aquí. {{plural_you:Pongan|Poned}} el pie sobre el cuello de estos reyes». Los jefes se acercaron y pusieron el pie sobre el cuello de los reyes.

decisions.choice: put your feet on the necks: a sign of complete victory
decisions.reason: A conqueror placing his foot on a defeated enemy showed that the enemy was wholly in his power (1 Kings 5:17; Psalm 110:1). Here it is done in front of all Israel, as a sign of what God will do (verse 25).

decisions.choice: commanders: officers who led the fighting men
decisions.reason: The word means a leader or chief, here the officers of the army.

decisions.choice: the commanders ... the kings' necks
decisions.reason: Readable names who came forward and whose necks are meant.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ אַל־תִּֽירְא֖וּ וְאַל־תֵּחָ֑תּוּ חִזְק֣וּ וְאִמְצ֔וּ כִּ֣י כָ֗כָה יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְכָל־אֹ֣יְבֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם נִלְחָמִ֥ים אוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Joshua, Do not fear and do not be dismayed; be strong and be bold, for thus will do Yahweh to all your enemies whom you [are] fighting them.

en.L: And Joshua said to them, "Do not fear, and do not be dismayed. Be strong and bold, for thus {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do to all your enemies whom you fight."
en.B: Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid or discouraged. Be strong and courageous, because this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do to all the enemies you fight."
en.R: Joshua told them, "Do not be afraid. Do not lose heart. Be strong and brave. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do to all the enemies you fight against."

sw.L: Yoshua akawaambia, "Msiogope wala msifadhaike; muwe imara na jasiri, kwa maana hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakavyowatendea adui zenu wote mnaopigana nao."
sw.B: Yoshua aliwaambia, "Msiogope wala msikate tamaa. Muwe imara na jasiri, kwa sababu hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakavyowatendea adui zenu wote mtakaopigana nao."
sw.R: Yoshua aliwaambia, "Msiogope. Msife moyo. Muwe imara na mashujaa. Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakavyowatendea adui zenu wote mtakaopigana nao."

es.L: Y Josué les dijo: «No {{plural_you:teman|temáis}}, y no {{plural_you:se acobarden|os acobardéis}}. {{plural_you:Sean fuertes y valerosos|Sed fuertes y valerosos}}, porque así hará {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a todos {{plural_you:sus enemigos|vuestros enemigos}} contra los que {{plural_you:pelean|peleáis}}».
es.B: Josué les dijo: «No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo ni {{plural_you:se desanimen|os desaniméis}}. {{plural_you:Sean fuertes y valientes|Sed fuertes y valientes}}, porque esto es lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hará con todos los enemigos contra los que {{plural_you:luchen|luchéis}}».
es.R: Josué les dijo: «No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. No {{plural_you:pierdan|perdáis}} el ánimo. {{plural_you:Sean fuertes y valientes|Sed fuertes y valientes}}. Esto es lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hará con todos los enemigos contra los que {{plural_you:peleen|peleéis}}».

decisions.choice: do not fear ... be strong and bold: God's words to Joshua passed on to the army
decisions.reason: God gave Joshua this charge in 1:6, 7, 9 and said "Do not fear and do not be dismayed" in 8:1. Joshua now says the same to his commanders.

decisions.choice: thus the LORD will do: what was done to these kings is a sign of what is to come
decisions.reason: The kings under the commanders' feet show what will happen to every enemy Israel fights.

decisions.choice: bold (Literal), courageous (Balanced), brave (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1:6.

source.text: וַיַּכֵּ֨ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵן֙ וַיְמִיתֵ֔ם וַיִּתְלֵ֕ם עַ֖ל חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה עֵצִ֑ים וַיִּֽהְי֛וּ תְּלוּיִ֥ם עַל־הָעֵצִ֖ים עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And struck them Joshua after so, and put them to death and hung them on five trees, and they were hanging on the trees until the evening.

en.L: And Joshua struck them afterward and put them to death, and he hung them on five trees, and they were hanging on the trees until the evening.
en.B: After this Joshua struck them down and put them to death, and he hung them on five trees. They stayed hanging on the trees until evening.
en.R: Then Joshua killed the kings and hung their bodies on five trees. They were left hanging there until evening.

sw.L: Baadaye Yoshua akawapiga, akawaua, akawatundika juu ya miti mitano; nao wakawa wametundikwa juu ya miti hadi jioni.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo Yoshua aliwapiga na kuwaua, akawatundika juu ya miti mitano. Walibaki wakining'inia mitini mpaka jioni.
sw.R: Kisha Yoshua aliwaua wale wafalme, akaitundika miili yao juu ya miti mitano. Iliachwa ikining'inia huko mpaka jioni.

es.L: Y después de esto Josué los hirió y les dio muerte, y los colgó en cinco árboles, y quedaron colgados en los árboles hasta la tarde.
es.B: Después Josué los hirió y les dio muerte, y los colgó de cinco árboles. Quedaron colgados de los árboles hasta la tarde.
es.R: Luego Josué mató a los reyes y colgó sus cuerpos de cinco árboles. Los dejaron colgados allí hasta la tarde.

decisions.choice: hung them on five trees: the dead bodies were displayed
decisions.reason: The kings were killed first and their bodies then hung up for all to see, as was done with the king of Ai (8:29). The word for "tree" can also mean a wooden post.

decisions.choice: their bodies
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the kings were already dead when they were hung up.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י לְעֵ֣ת׀בּ֣וֹא הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ צִוָּ֤ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ וַיֹּֽרִידוּם֙ מֵעַ֣ל הָעֵצִ֔ים וַיַּ֨שְׁלִכֻ֔ם אֶל־הַמְּעָרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר נֶחְבְּאוּ־שָׁ֑ם וַיָּשִׂ֜מוּ אֲבָנִ֤ים גְּדֹלוֹת֙ עַל־פִּ֣י הַמְּעָרָ֔ה עַד־עֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it was, at [the] time of [the] going of the sun, commanded Joshua, and they took them down from on the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden themselves there, and they put stones great on [the] mouth of the cave, until [the] very day the this.

en.L: And it happened at the time of the setting of the sun [that] Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden themselves, and they put large stones over the mouth of the cave, until this very day.
en.B: At sunset Joshua gave the order, and they took the bodies down from the trees and threw them into the cave where the kings had hidden. They placed large stones over the mouth of the cave, and they remain there to this very day.
en.R: When the sun was going down, Joshua gave orders. His men took the bodies down from the trees and threw them into the cave where the kings had hidden. They put big stones over the opening of the cave. Those stones are still there today.

sw.L: Ikawa wakati wa kuzama kwa jua Yoshua akaamuru, wakawashusha kutoka mitini, wakawatupa katika pango walimojificha, wakaweka mawe makubwa kwenye mdomo wa pango, hadi siku hii hii ya leo.
sw.B: Jua lilipozama Yoshua alitoa amri, nao wakaishusha miili kutoka mitini, wakaitupa ndani ya pango walimokuwa wamejificha wafalme. Waliweka mawe makubwa juu ya mdomo wa pango, nayo yako hapo hata leo.
sw.R: Jua lilipokuwa likizama, Yoshua alitoa amri. Watu wake waliishusha miili kutoka mitini, wakaitupa ndani ya pango walimokuwa wamejificha wafalme. Waliweka mawe makubwa mbele ya mlango wa pango. Mawe hayo bado yako hapo leo.

es.L: Y sucedió a la hora de ponerse el sol [que] Josué dio la orden, y los bajaron de los árboles y los echaron en la cueva donde se habían escondido, y pusieron grandes piedras a la boca de la cueva, hasta este mismo día.
es.B: A la puesta del sol, Josué dio la orden, y bajaron los cuerpos de los árboles y los echaron en la cueva donde los reyes se habían escondido. Pusieron grandes piedras en la boca de la cueva, y allí siguen hasta el día de hoy.
es.R: Cuando se estaba poniendo el sol, Josué dio órdenes. Sus hombres bajaron los cuerpos de los árboles y los echaron en la cueva donde los reyes se habían escondido. Pusieron piedras grandes en la entrada de la cueva. Esas piedras todavía están allí hoy.

decisions.choice: at sunset ... they took them down: the law of Deuteronomy 21:22-23
decisions.reason: The law said that a body hung on a tree must not stay there overnight. Joshua kept it here, as at Ai (8:29). On "the going of the sun" meaning sunset, see verse 13.

decisions.choice: until this very day: in the writer's own day
decisions.reason: The stones over the cave were still there when the book was written, as with the heap of stones over the king of Ai (8:29).

decisions.choice: the stones are there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what remained "until this very day".

source.text: וְאֶת־מַקֵּדָה֩ לָכַ֨ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיַּכֶּ֣הָ לְפִי־חֶרֶב֮ וְאֶת־מַלְכָּהּ֒ הֶחֱרִ֣ם אוֹתָ֗ם וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֨פֶשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א הִשְׁאִ֖יר שָׂרִ֑יד וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מַקֵּדָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ יְרִיחֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Makkedah captured Joshua on the day the that, and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword, and its king; he devoted to destruction them and every person who [was] in it; not he left a survivor; and he did to [the] king of Makkedah just as he had done to [the] king of Jericho.

en.L: And Joshua captured Makkedah on that day, and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king. He devoted them to destruction, and every person who [was] in it; he did not leave a survivor. And he did to the king of Makkedah just as he had done to the king of Jericho.
en.B: Joshua captured Makkedah that same day. He struck it down with the sword, together with its king, and devoted them to destruction with everyone in it. He left no survivors. He did to the king of Makkedah what he had done to the king of Jericho.
en.R: That same day Joshua captured Makkedah. He struck it down with the sword, together with its king. He destroyed them completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with everyone in it. He left no one alive. He did to the king of Makkedah what he had done to the king of Jericho.

sw.L: Na Makeda Yoshua aliuteka siku ile, akaupiga kwa makali ya upanga, na mfalme wake. Akawaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi, na kila mtu aliyekuwamo; hakumwacha aliyenusurika. Akamtendea mfalme wa Makeda kama alivyomtendea mfalme wa Yeriko.
sw.B: Siku ile ile Yoshua aliuteka Makeda. Aliupiga kwa upanga pamoja na mfalme wake, akawaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi pamoja na kila mtu aliyekuwamo. Hakumwacha hata mmoja aliyenusurika. Alimtendea mfalme wa Makeda kama alivyomtendea mfalme wa Yeriko.
sw.R: Siku ile ile Yoshua aliuteka Makeda. Aliupiga kwa upanga pamoja na mfalme wake. Aliwaangamiza kabisa, kama watu waliotolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, pamoja na kila mtu aliyekuwamo. Hakumwacha mtu yeyote hai. Alimtendea mfalme wa Makeda kama alivyomtendea mfalme wa Yeriko.

es.L: Y Josué tomó Maceda aquel día, y la hirió a filo de espada, y a su rey. Los consagró al exterminio, y a toda persona que [había] en ella; no dejó sobreviviente. E hizo al rey de Maceda como había hecho al rey de Jericó.
es.B: Josué tomó Maceda ese mismo día. La pasó a espada, junto con su rey, y los consagró al exterminio con todos los que había en ella. No dejó sobrevivientes. Hizo con el rey de Maceda lo que había hecho con el rey de Jericó.
es.R: Ese mismo día Josué tomó Maceda. La atacó a espada, junto con su rey. Los destruyó por completo, como entregados {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, con todos los que había en ella. No dejó a nadie con vida. Hizo con el rey de Maceda lo que había hecho con el rey de Jericó.

decisions.choice: devoted them to destruction: the town and its people were given over to God completely
decisions.reason: As in verse 1 and 6:17, 21. The command is given in Deuteronomy 7:2 and 20:16-17. "Them" means the king and the people of the town.

decisions.choice: with the mouth of the sword: by the sword, killing in battle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the sword's "mouth", the edge that "eats" (2 Samuel 2:26). The phrase means to kill with the sword, without sparing.

decisions.choice: as he had done to the king of Jericho: the pattern set at the first city
decisions.reason: Jericho and its king were given over to Joshua (6:2) and destroyed (6:21); Ai and its king followed the same pattern (8:2, 29). Verses 28-39 repeat the same words city after city.

decisions.choice: destroyed them completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 1. Readable uses the same words for this term each time it appears in verses 28-40.

decisions.choice: the repeated phrases of verses 28-39 are worded the same each time
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a fixed set of phrases for each city taken ("struck it with the edge of the sword", "left no survivor", "did to its king as ..."). Each level keeps one wording for each phrase throughout, so the repetition can be heard. Balanced "left no survivors" is Readable "left no one alive". The move from town to town is worded the same way too: Literal "Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from ... to ...", Balanced "Next Joshua advanced from ... to ... with all Israel", Readable "Then Joshua and all Israel went on from ... to ...".

decisions.choice: the same Swahili wording each time the account repeats itself in verses 28-39
decisions.reason: The Hebrew tells the taking of each town in the same set phrases, and the English keeps them the same; Swahili does too ("aliupiga kwa upanga", "hakumwacha hata mmoja aliyenusurika", "kama alivyomtendea"), so that the pattern can be heard.

decisions.choice: one wording for each repeated phrase of verses 28-39
decisions.reason: Like the English, each level keeps one Spanish wording for each of the fixed phrases used of every city taken: Literal "la hirió a filo de espada" and "no dejó sobreviviente"; Balanced "la pasó a espada" and "no dejó sobrevivientes"; Readable "la atacó a espada" and "no dejó a nadie con vida".

source.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מִמַּקֵּדָ֖ה לִבְנָ֑ה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם עִם־לִבְנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And passed on Joshua and all Israel with him from Makkedah [to] Libnah, and fought with Libnah.

en.L: And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Makkedah to Libnah, and he fought against Libnah.
en.B: Next Joshua advanced from Makkedah to Libnah with all Israel and attacked Libnah.
en.R: Then Joshua and all Israel went on from Makkedah to Libnah and attacked Libnah.

sw.L: Yoshua akapita, na Israeli wote pamoja naye, kutoka Makeda hadi Libna, akapigana na Libna.
sw.B: Kisha Yoshua, pamoja na Israeli wote, alisonga mbele kutoka Makeda hadi Libna, akaushambulia Libna.
sw.R: Kisha Yoshua na Israeli wote walikwenda kutoka Makeda hadi Libna, wakaushambulia Libna.

es.L: Y pasó Josué, y todo Israel con él, de Maceda a Libná, y combatió contra Libná.
es.B: Luego Josué avanzó de Maceda a Libná con todo Israel y atacó Libná.
es.R: Luego Josué y todo Israel siguieron de Maceda a Libná y atacaron Libná.

decisions.choice: Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron, Debir: the towns of the southern campaign
decisions.reason: From Makkedah the army moved through towns of the low hills to the southwest (Libnah, Lachish, Eglon), then turned up into the hill country (Hebron, Debir). The exact site of some of these towns is not certain.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה גַּם־אוֹתָ֜הּ בְּיַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֘לוְאֶת־מַלְכָּהּ֒ וַיַּכֶּ֣הָ לְפִי־חֶ֗רֶב וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֨פֶשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔הּ לֹֽא־הִשְׁאִ֥יר בָּ֖הּ שָׂרִ֑יד וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לְמַלְכָּ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ יְרִיחֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And gave Yahweh also it into [the] hand of Israel and its king, and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword and every person who [was] in it; not he left in it a survivor; and he did to its king just as he had done to [the] king of Jericho.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave it also, and its king, into the hand of Israel, and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who [was] in it; he did not leave a survivor in it. And he did to its king just as he had done to the king of Jericho.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} handed it and its king over to Israel as well. He struck it down with the sword, with everyone in it. He left no survivors. He did to its king what he had done to the king of Jericho.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} handed it and its king over to Israel too. He struck it down with the sword, with everyone in it. He left no one alive. He did to its king what he had done to the king of Jericho.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akautia huo pia, na mfalme wake, mkononi mwa Israeli; akaupiga kwa makali ya upanga, na kila mtu aliyekuwamo; hakumwacha ndani yake aliyenusurika. Akamtendea mfalme wake kama alivyomtendea mfalme wa Yeriko.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliutia huo pia pamoja na mfalme wake mikononi mwa Israeli. Aliupiga kwa upanga pamoja na kila mtu aliyekuwamo. Hakumwacha hata mmoja aliyenusurika. Alimtendea mfalme wake kama alivyomtendea mfalme wa Yeriko.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliutia huo pia pamoja na mfalme wake mikononi mwa Israeli. Aliupiga kwa upanga pamoja na kila mtu aliyekuwamo. Hakumwacha mtu yeyote hai. Alimtendea mfalme wake kama alivyomtendea mfalme wa Yeriko.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} la entregó también, a ella y a su rey, en mano de Israel, y la hirió a filo de espada, y a toda persona que [había] en ella; no dejó en ella sobreviviente. E hizo a su rey como había hecho al rey de Jericó.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} la entregó también a ella y a su rey en manos de Israel. Josué la pasó a espada, con todos los que había en ella. No dejó sobrevivientes. Hizo con su rey lo que había hecho con el rey de Jericó.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entregó también la ciudad y a su rey en manos de Israel. Josué la atacó a espada, con todos los que había en ella. No dejó a nadie con vida. Hizo con su rey lo que había hecho con el rey de Jericó.

decisions.choice: he struck it: Joshua, now the subject again
decisions.reason: The LORD gives the city into Israel's hand; Joshua and the army strike it. In verses 28-39 the Hebrew moves between "he" (Joshua) and "they" (Joshua and Israel) with no change in meaning.

decisions.choice: gave into the hand of Israel: handed over to Israel's power
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

source.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מִלִּבְנָ֖ה לָכִ֑ישָׁה וַיִּ֣חַן עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And passed on Joshua and all Israel with him from Libnah to Lachish, and encamped against it and fought against it.

en.L: And Joshua passed on, and all Israel with him, from Libnah to Lachish, and he camped against it and fought against it.
en.B: Next Joshua advanced from Libnah to Lachish with all Israel. He camped against it and attacked it.
en.R: Then Joshua and all Israel went on from Libnah to Lachish. He camped around it and attacked it.

sw.L: Yoshua akapita, na Israeli wote pamoja naye, kutoka Libna hadi Lakishi, akapiga kambi kuukabili, akapigana nao.
sw.B: Kisha Yoshua, pamoja na Israeli wote, alisonga mbele kutoka Libna hadi Lakishi. Alipiga kambi kuukabili, akaushambulia.
sw.R: Kisha Yoshua na Israeli wote walikwenda kutoka Libna hadi Lakishi. Alipiga kambi kuuzunguka, akaushambulia.

es.L: Y pasó Josué, y todo Israel con él, de Libná a Laquis, y acampó contra ella y la combatió.
es.B: Luego Josué avanzó de Libná a Laquis con todo Israel. Acampó frente a ella y la atacó.
es.R: Luego Josué y todo Israel siguieron de Libná a Laquis. Acampó alrededor de la ciudad y la atacó.

decisions.choice: camped against it: laid siege to the city
decisions.reason: The army set up camp before the walls in order to take the city (verse 5).

source.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶת־לָכִ֜ישׁ בְּיַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַֽיִּלְכְּדָהּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וַיַּכֶּ֣הָ לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֑הּ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה לְלִבְנָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And gave Yahweh Lachish into [the] hand of Israel, and he captured it on the day the second, and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword and every person who [was] in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the second day, and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who [was] in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} handed Lachish over to Israel, and he captured it on the second day. He struck it down with the sword, with everyone in it, just as he had done to Libnah.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} handed Lachish over to Israel, and he captured it on the second day. He struck it down with the sword, with everyone in it, just as he had done to Libnah.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akautia Lakishi mkononi mwa Israeli, akauteka siku ya pili, akaupiga kwa makali ya upanga, na kila mtu aliyekuwamo, sawasawa na yote aliyoufanyia Libna.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliutia Lakishi mikononi mwa Israeli, naye akauteka siku ya pili. Aliupiga kwa upanga pamoja na kila mtu aliyekuwamo, kama alivyoufanyia Libna.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliutia Lakishi mikononi mwa Israeli, naye akauteka siku ya pili. Aliupiga kwa upanga pamoja na kila mtu aliyekuwamo, kama alivyoufanyia Libna.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entregó Laquis en mano de Israel, y la tomó al segundo día, y la hirió a filo de espada, y a toda persona que [había] en ella, conforme a todo lo que había hecho a Libná.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entregó Laquis en manos de Israel, y Josué la tomó al segundo día. La pasó a espada, con todos los que había en ella, tal como había hecho con Libná.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entregó Laquis en manos de Israel, y Josué la tomó al segundo día. La atacó a espada, con todos los que había en ella, tal como había hecho con Libná.

decisions.choice: on the second day: Lachish held out longer than the other towns
decisions.reason: Lachish was one of the strongest walled cities of the region. The other towns are taken "on that day" (verses 28, 35).

source.text: אָ֣ז עָלָ֗ה הֹרָם֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ גֶּ֔זֶר לַעְזֹ֖ר אֶת־לָכִ֑ישׁ וַיַּכֵּ֤הוּ יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ וְאֶת־עַמּ֔וֹ עַד־בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־ל֖וֹ שָׂרִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: Then came up Horam king of Gezer to help Lachish, and struck him Joshua and his people until not he left to him a survivor.

en.L: Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people, until he did not leave him a survivor.
en.B: At that time Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, but Joshua defeated him and his army, leaving him no survivors.
en.R: Then Horam, the king of Gezer, came to help Lachish. But Joshua defeated him and his army. He left no one alive.

sw.L: Ndipo Horamu mfalme wa Gezeri akapanda kuusaidia Lakishi, naye Yoshua akampiga yeye na watu wake, mpaka hakumwachia aliyenusurika.
sw.B: Wakati huo Horamu mfalme wa Gezeri alipanda kuusaidia Lakishi, lakini Yoshua alimshinda yeye na jeshi lake, asimwachie hata mmoja aliyenusurika.
sw.R: Kisha Horamu, mfalme wa Gezeri, alikuja kuusaidia Lakishi. Lakini Yoshua alimshinda yeye na jeshi lake. Hakumwacha mtu yeyote hai.

es.L: Entonces Horam, rey de Guézer, subió para ayudar a Laquis, y Josué lo hirió a él y a su pueblo, hasta no dejarle sobreviviente.
es.B: En ese tiempo Horam, rey de Guézer, subió para ayudar a Laquis, pero Josué lo derrotó a él y a su ejército, sin dejarle sobrevivientes.
es.R: Entonces Horam, rey de Guézer, vino a ayudar a Laquis. Pero Josué lo derrotó a él y a su ejército. No dejó a nadie con vida.

decisions.choice: Horam king of Gezer: a king from the northwest
decisions.reason: Gezer lay to the northwest, on the edge of the low hills. Only its king and his army are said to be defeated; the town itself was not taken, and Canaanites still lived there later (16:10).

decisions.choice: his people: his army
decisions.reason: "People" often means the fighting men (verses 7, 21).

decisions.choice: defeated him and his army
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "defeated" for "struck", since a king and his army in the field are meant, and "army" for "people" (m2).

en.B: Next Joshua advanced from Lachish to Eglon with all Israel. They camped against it and attacked it.
en.R: Then Joshua and all Israel went on from Lachish to Eglon. They camped around it and attacked it.

es.B: Luego Josué avanzó de Laquis a Eglón con todo Israel. Acamparon frente a ella y la atacaron.
es.R: Luego Josué y todo Israel siguieron de Laquis a Eglón. Acamparon alrededor de la ciudad y la atacaron.

decisions.choice: they camped: Joshua and all Israel
decisions.reason: As in verse 30: the Hebrew changes from "he" to "they" here without any change in meaning.

records.literal_gloss: And they captured it on the day the that, and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword, and every person who [was] in it on the day the that he devoted to destruction, according to all that he had done to Lachish.

en.L: And they captured it on that day, and they struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person who [was] in it he devoted to destruction on that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
en.B: They captured it that same day and struck it down with the sword. He devoted everyone in it to destruction that day, just as he had done to Lachish.
en.R: They captured it that same day and struck it down with the sword. That day he destroyed everyone in it completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as he had done to Lachish.

sw.L: Wakauteka siku ile, wakaupiga kwa makali ya upanga, na kila mtu aliyekuwamo akamweka wakfu kwa maangamizi siku ile, sawasawa na yote aliyoufanyia Lakishi.
sw.B: Waliuteka siku ile ile, wakaupiga kwa upanga. Siku ile aliwaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi wote waliokuwamo, kama alivyoufanyia Lakishi.
sw.R: Waliuteka siku ile ile, wakaupiga kwa upanga. Siku ile aliwaangamiza kabisa wote waliokuwamo, kama watu waliotolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kama alivyoufanyia Lakishi.

es.L: Y la tomaron aquel día, y la hirieron a filo de espada, y a toda persona que [había] en ella la consagró al exterminio aquel día, conforme a todo lo que había hecho a Laquis.
es.B: La tomaron ese mismo día y la pasaron a espada. Aquel día consagró al exterminio a todos los que había en ella, tal como había hecho con Laquis.
es.R: La tomaron ese mismo día y la atacaron a espada. Aquel día Josué destruyó por completo a todos los que había en ella, como entregados {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, tal como había hecho con Laquis.

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

records.literal_gloss: And went up Joshua and all Israel with him from Eglon to Hebron, and they fought against it.

en.B: Next Joshua went up from Eglon to Hebron with all Israel and attacked it.
en.R: Then Joshua and all Israel went up from Eglon to Hebron and attacked it.

sw.L: Yoshua akapanda, na Israeli wote pamoja naye, kutoka Egloni hadi Hebroni, wakapigana nao.
sw.B: Kisha Yoshua, pamoja na Israeli wote, alipanda kutoka Egloni hadi Hebroni, akaushambulia.
sw.R: Kisha Yoshua na Israeli wote walipanda kutoka Egloni hadi Hebroni, wakaushambulia.

es.L: Y subió Josué, y todo Israel con él, de Eglón a Hebrón, y la combatieron.
es.B: Luego Josué subió de Eglón a Hebrón con todo Israel y la atacó.
es.R: Luego Josué y todo Israel subieron de Eglón a Hebrón y la atacaron.

decisions.choice: went up: from the low hills into the hill country
decisions.reason: Hebron stands high in the hills of Judah, well above Eglon.

source.text: וַיִּלְכְּד֣וּהָ וַיַּכּֽוּהָ־לְפִי־חֶ֠רֶב וְאֶת־מַלְכָּ֨הּ וְאֶת־כָּל־עָרֶ֜יהָ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּהּ֙ לֹֽא־הִשְׁאִ֣יר שָׂרִ֔יד כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה לְעֶגְל֑וֹן וַיַּחֲרֵ֣ם אוֹתָ֔הּ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּֽהּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they captured it and struck it with [the] mouth of [the] sword, and its king and all its cities and every person who [was] in it; not he left a survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon; and he devoted to destruction it and every person who [was] in it.

en.L: And they captured it, and they struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king and all its towns and every person who [was] in it; he did not leave a survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon. And he devoted it to destruction, and every person who [was] in it.
en.B: They captured it and struck it down with the sword, together with its king, its towns and everyone in it. He left no survivors, just as he had done to Eglon. He devoted it to destruction with everyone in it.
en.R: They captured it and struck it down with the sword, together with its king, the towns around it and everyone in it. He left no one alive, just as he had done to Eglon. He destroyed it completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with everyone in it.

sw.L: Wakauteka, wakaupiga kwa makali ya upanga, na mfalme wake na miji yake yote na kila mtu aliyekuwamo; hakumwacha aliyenusurika, sawasawa na yote aliyoufanyia Egloni. Akauweka wakfu kwa maangamizi, na kila mtu aliyekuwamo.
sw.B: Waliuteka, wakaupiga kwa upanga pamoja na mfalme wake, miji yake na kila mtu aliyekuwamo. Hakumwacha hata mmoja aliyenusurika, kama alivyoufanyia Egloni. Aliuweka wakfu kwa maangamizi pamoja na kila mtu aliyekuwamo.
sw.R: Waliuteka, wakaupiga kwa upanga pamoja na mfalme wake, miji iliyouzunguka na kila mtu aliyekuwamo. Hakumwacha mtu yeyote hai, kama alivyoufanyia Egloni. Aliuangamiza kabisa, kama watu waliotolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, pamoja na kila mtu aliyekuwamo.

es.L: Y la tomaron, y la hirieron a filo de espada, y a su rey y a todas sus ciudades y a toda persona que [había] en ella; no dejó sobreviviente, conforme a todo lo que había hecho a Eglón. Y la consagró al exterminio, y a toda persona que [había] en ella.
es.B: La tomaron y la pasaron a espada, junto con su rey, sus ciudades y todos los que había en ella. No dejó sobrevivientes, tal como había hecho con Eglón. La consagró al exterminio con todos los que había en ella.
es.R: La tomaron y la atacaron a espada, junto con su rey, los pueblos de alrededor y todos los que había en ella. No dejó a nadie con vida, tal como había hecho con Eglón. La destruyó por completo, como entregada {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, con todos los que había en ella.

decisions.choice: its king: a king of Hebron after the one killed at Makkedah
alternatives: the repeated pattern, not a second king
decisions.reason: The king of Hebron was put to death at Makkedah (verses 23, 26). The king here may be one who had taken his place, or the phrase may follow the pattern of the other cities without naming a new king.

decisions.choice: all its cities: the smaller towns and villages that belonged to Hebron
decisions.reason: A main city ruled the towns of the land around it (15:44-45, "its towns and villages").

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

decisions.choice: the towns around it; destroyed ... completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what "its cities" were (m2) and explains the term as in verse 28.

source.text: וַיָּ֧שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֖וֹ דְּבִ֑רָה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם עָלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned Joshua and all Israel with him [to] Debir, and fought against it.

en.L: And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to Debir, and he fought against it.
en.B: Next Joshua turned back to Debir with all Israel and attacked it.
en.R: Then Joshua and all Israel turned back to Debir and attacked it.

records.literal_gloss: And he captured it and its king and all its cities, and they struck them with [the] mouth of [the] sword and devoted to destruction every person who [was] in it; not he left a survivor; just as he had done to Hebron so he did to Debir and to its king, and just as he had done to Libnah and to its king.

en.L: And he captured it and its king and all its towns, and they struck them with the edge of the sword, and they devoted to destruction every person who [was] in it; he did not leave a survivor.
